children.translated_text: A certain <s>Yakṣa</s>, negligent in his duties due to the burden of separation from his beloved,
his glory eclipsed by a curse from his master that was to last a year,
made his dwelling among the waters sanctified by <s>Sītā</s>'s bathing, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
in the hermitages of <s>Rāmagiri</s>, beneath trees of loving shade.

children.text: tasminn adrau kati cid abalāviprayuktaḥ sa kāmī
children.translated_text: On that mountain, that lover, separated from his wife for some months,
his wrists left bare by the slipping of his golden bracelets,
on the calming day of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, beheld a cloud embracing the peak,
magnificent as a mature elephant playfully butting a rampart.

children.text: tasya sthitvā katham api puraḥ ketakādhānahetor
children.translated_text: Standing before it somehow, as if to offer <s>ketaka</s> (screw-pine) flowers,
the servant of the king of kings, suppressing tears within, reflected long—
at the sight of a cloud, even the heart of one who is happy turns to other thoughts;
how much more so for one whose beloved, fond of neck-embraces, dwells far away.
As the rainy season drew near, longing to sustain his beloved's life,
he resolved to send through the cloud a message of his own well-being.
He, having prepared an offering of fresh <s>kuṭaja</s> blossoms for that cloud,
joyfully spoke a word of welcome, with affection at the fore.
Where is a cloud—a mere confluence of smoke, light, water, and wind—
and where are messages, to be delivered by sentient beings of keen faculties?

children.text: ity autsukyād aparigaṇayan guhyakas taṃ yayāce
children.translated_text: Yet the <s>Guhyaka</s> (Yakṣa), not weighing this in his eagerness, implored it—
for those afflicted by desire, wretched in love, cannot distinguish the sentient from the insentient.
Born in the world-renowned lineage of <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> clouds,
I know you to be a chief servant of <s>Maghon</s> (<s>Indra</s>), able to assume any form at will.
Therefore I, a kinsman separated by fate's decree, have come to you as a supplicant—

children.text: yācñā vandhyā varam adhiguṇe nādhame labdhakāmā
children.translated_text: a plea made to one of superior qualities is better fruitless than a wish granted by the base.

children.text: saṃtaptānāṃ tvam asi śaraṇaṃ tat payoda priyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: You are the refuge of the scorched; therefore, O cloud, carry to my beloved
my message—I who have been separated by the wrath of <s>Kubera</s>, lord of wealth.

children.text: gantavyā te vasatir alakā nāma yakṣeśvarāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: You must travel to the dwelling named <s>Alakā</s>, city of the <s>Yakṣa</s> lords,
whose mansions are washed white by the moonlight from <s>Śiva</s>'s head, who resides in the outer gardens.
When you have mounted the pathway of the wind, women of travelers, their loosened hair uplifted,
will gaze upon you, drawing hope and comfort from the sight.

children.text: kaḥ saṃnaddhe virahavidhurāṃ tvayy upekṣeta jāyāṃ
children.translated_text: Who, when you are girded for your journey, would neglect a wife distressed by separation?

children.text: na syād anyo 'py aham iva jano yaḥ parādhīnavṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: There could be no other soul like me, whose fate is governed by another's will.

children.text: āpṛcchasva priyasakham amuṃ tuṅgam āliṅgya śailaṃ
children.translated_text: Take leave of this lofty mountain, your dear friend, embracing it,
whose girdle-slopes are marked by the footprints of <s>Raghupati</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), venerable to all men.

children.text: kāle kāle bhavati bhavatā yasya saṃyogam etya
children.translated_text: Season after season, when you come to meet him,
your bond of affection is made manifest—he sheds hot tears born of long separation.

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ nudati pavanaś cānukūlo yathā tvāṃ
children.translated_text: The wind gently, gently urges you onward in a favorable direction,

children.text: vāmaś cāyaṃ nadati madhuraṃ cātakas toyagṛdhnuḥ
children.translated_text: and on your left the <s>cātaka</s> bird, thirsting for raindrops, sings sweetly.
Surely the <s>balākā</s> (cranes), steadied by the familiarity of bearing your offspring, forming garlands,
will attend upon you in the sky, a delight to behold.
And her you shall surely see—that faithful wife, counting each day with devotion,
your brother's wife, unharmed, if your passage is unimpeded.
For hope's tender bond, fragile as a blossom, is what mostly
sustains the heart of women in separation, a heart ever ready to fall.

children.text: kartuṃ yac ca prabhavati mahīm ucchilindhrām avandhyaṃ
children.translated_text: And hearing your thunder, delightful to the ear, which has the power

children.text: tac chrutvā te śravaṇasubhagaṃ garjitaṃ mānasotkāḥ
children.translated_text: to make the earth fruitful and bristling with mushrooms,
the royal swans, eager for <s>Mānasa</s> lake, provisioned with lotus-stalk fibers,
will become your companions in the sky, all the way to <s>Kailāsa</s>.
First hear me describe the route favorable to your journey,

children.text: saṃdeśaṃ me tadanu jalada śroṣyasi śrotrapeyam
children.translated_text: and then, O rain-cloud, you shall hear my message, sweet as nectar to the ear.

children.text: khinnaḥ khinnaḥ śikhariṣu padaṃ nyasya gantāsi yatra
children.translated_text: Where, weary and weary again, you shall rest your foot upon the peaks,

children.text: kṣīṇaḥ kṣīṇaḥ parilaghu payaḥ srotasāṃ copabhujya
children.translated_text: and, depleted and depleted, refresh yourself lightly from the currents of streams.

children.text: adreḥ śṛṅgaṃ harati pavanaḥ kiṃ svid ity unmukhībhir
children.translated_text: While the innocent <s>Siddha</s>-women gaze with upturned faces, wondering
'Is the wind carrying off the mountain peak?'—startled yet emboldened by the sight—
rise upward from this place, lush with reeds, northward into the sky,
avoiding on the path of the directional elephants the licking of their thick trunks.
Before you, like an interplay of jewel-lights, you shall see
a fragment of <s>Indra</s>'s bow rising from the tip of an anthill.

children.text: yena śyāmaṃ vapur atitarāṃ kāntim āpatsyate te
children.translated_text: By which your dark form will attain surpassing beauty,
as does <s>Viṣṇu</s> in his cowherd guise adorned with a gleaming peacock feather.
By the eyes of country women, tender with affection, unknowing of coquettish frowns,
you shall be drunk in, for the harvest depends upon you.
Ascending the <s>Māla</s> plateau, fragrant with freshly ploughed fields,

children.text: kiṃ cit paścād pravalaya gatiṃ bhūya evottareṇa
children.translated_text: slow your pace a little, then press onward again to the north.
<s>Āmrakūṭa</s>, that mountain with its ridges, will properly welcome you upon its summit,
weary from travel, you who have stilled the forest fires with your showers.
Not even the lowliest, mindful of past kindnesses, turns away

children.text: prāpte mitre bhavati vimukhaḥ kiṃ punar yas tathoccaiḥ
children.translated_text: when a friend arrives seeking shelter—how much less one so exalted.
Its borders hidden by forest mango trees radiant with ripe fruit,
when you have mounted its peak, dark as a glossy braid of hair,
the mountain will surely assume a form worthy of beholding by the immortal couples—

children.text: madhye śyāmaḥ stana iva bhuvaḥ śeṣavistārapāṇḍuḥ
children.translated_text: dark in the middle like a breast of the earth, pale with expanse on every side.
Having rested a moment in a bower enjoyed by forest-dwelling women,
quickening your pace with the release of rain, crossing the path beyond,
you shall see the <s>Revā</s> (Narmadā) scattered across the rocky foot of the <s>Vindhya</s>,

children.text: bhakticchedair iva viracitāṃ bhūtim aṅge gajasya
children.translated_text: as if the ornamental streaks painted on the body of an elephant were broken apart.
Having shed your rain, take up her water, scented with the pungent ichor of wild elephants,
its flow checked by thickets of <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) trees, and proceed.

children.text: antaḥsāraṃ ghana tulayituṃ nānilaḥ śakṣyati tvāṃ
children.translated_text: The wind will not be able to weigh you as hollow within, O dense cloud—

children.text: riktaḥ sarvo bhavati hi laghuḥ pūrṇatā gauravāya
children.translated_text: for everything empty is light; it is fullness that gives weight.
Seeing the <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) trees, tawny-green with half-opened stamens,
and the <s>kandalī</s> (plantain) plants with their first buds just appearing along the banks,
smelling the earth's fragrance, intensely sweet in burnt-out forests,
the <s>sāraṅga</s> deer will point out your path, O releaser of rain-drops.

children.text: utpaśyāmi drutam api sakhe matpriyārthaṃ yiyāsoḥ
children.translated_text: I foresee, dear friend, that even as you hasten for my beloved's sake,
there will be delays upon mountain after mountain, fragrant with <s>kakubha</s> (Arjuna) trees.
The peacocks, greeting you with cries and eyes moist with tears of joy, their glances pale-edged,

children.text: pratyudyātaḥ katham api bhavān gantum āśu vyavasyet
children.translated_text: will come forth to meet you—yet somehow you must resolve to move on swiftly.
With pale-canopied groves of <s>ketaka</s> (screw-pine) split open by their thorns,
with village shrines bustling from the nesting of house-sparrows fed on offerings,
with <s>jambū</s> forests dark with ripened fruit at their borders—
the <s>Daśārṇa</s> lands, where the geese linger but a few more days, shall come into your reach.
Going to their capital, renowned as <s>Vidiśā</s>,

children.text: gatvā sadyaḥ phalam avikalaṃ kāmukatvasya labdhā
children.translated_text: you will at once obtain the full reward of being a lover.
You shall drink the sweet water of the <s>Vetravatī</s>, lovely with the murmur at its banks,

children.text: sabhrūbhaṅgaṃ mukham iva payo vetravatyāś calormi
children.translated_text: its waves like a face with furrowed brows.
There you shall rest upon the hill called <s>Nīcais</s>, for the sake of repose,
which, by your contact, seems to bristle with its full-bloomed <s>kadamba</s> trees.
That hill which, through its stone pavilions fragrant with the perfume of courtesans' lovemaking,
proclaims the unbridled youth of its citizens.
Rested, proceed, sprinkling with fresh raindrops the jasmine trellises
of the gardens born along the banks of forest streams.
You will become briefly familiar to the women whose weary ears bear <s>utpala</s> lotuses
wilting from wiping the sweat of their cheeks—familiar through the gift of shade, though they turn their flower-faces away.

children.text: vakraḥ panthā yad api bhavataḥ prasthitasyottarāśāṃ
children.translated_text: Though your path curves as you set forth northward,
do not spurn the terrace-laps of <s>Ujjayinī</s> in disdain.
If you do not delight there in the sidelong glances of the city's women,

children.text: lolāpāṅgair yadi na ramase locanair vañcito 'si
children.translated_text: startled by the flashing of your lightning-garlands, with their trembling eyes, then you are deceived.
Meeting the <s>Nirvindhyā</s> river on your path, whose rows of birds cry out, disturbed by her waves, like the tinkling of a girdle,
who glides along revealing her navel-whirlpool with a stumbling grace,
become intimate with her innermost currents,

children.text: strīṇām ādyaṃ praṇayavacanaṃ vibhramo hi priyeṣu
children.translated_text: for a woman's first word of love to her beloved is but a coy dissembling.
Having passed beyond her, the <s>Sindhu</s> river, its waters braided into a single stream,
pale-shadowed with withered leaves falling from the trees upon its banks,
revealing in the state of separation her former beauty, O handsome one—

children.text: kārśyaṃ yena tyajati vidhinā sa tvayaivopapādyaḥ
children.translated_text: the means by which she may shed her emaciation must be furnished by you yourself.
Reaching <s>Avantī</s>, whose village elders are versed in the tales of <s>Udayana</s>,
follow the path to that city described before—<s>Viśālā</s>, the illustrious and vast.
It is as though a single radiant fragment of heaven were brought down

children.text: śeṣaiḥ puṇyair hṛtam iva divaḥ kāntimat khaṇḍam ekam
children.translated_text: by the remaining merits of the celestial beings who had exhausted the fruits of their good deeds.
Prolonging the resonant, passion-sweetened cries of the <s>sārasa</s> (crane) birds at dawn,
astringent with the friendly fragrance of lotuses blooming at daybreak,
where the breeze from the <s>Siprā</s> river, soothing to the limbs, removes the languor of lovemaking—
like a most beloved one, coaxing with the flattery of entreaty.
Your form nourished by the incense-smoke of hair-dressing wafting through latticed windows,
honored with a dance-offering by the household peacocks out of kinship's affection,
in the fragrant, flower-scented mansions of that city, you, weary traveler at heart—
having spent the night upon the roof-terraces marked with lac-dye from the feet of graceful women,

children.text: bhartuḥ kaṇṭhacchavir iti gaṇaiḥ sādaraṃ dṛśyamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: regarded with reverence by the <s>Gaṇas</s> as 'the lustre of our Lord's throat' —
you should proceed to the sacred abode of <s>Caṇḍeśvara</s>, lord of the three worlds,
its gardens shaken by the breezes of the <s>Gandhavatī</s>, fragrant with the pollen of blue lotuses,
breezes made cool by the bathing of young women engrossed in water-play.

children.text: apy anyasmiñ jaladhara mahākālam āsādya kāle
children.translated_text: At another time too, O cloud, having reached <s>Mahākāla</s>,

children.text: sthātavyaṃ te nayanaviṣayaṃ yāvad abhyeti bhānuḥ
children.translated_text: you must linger there until the sun enters the field of vision,
making praiseworthy the evening oblation with the drum-beat for the Trident-bearer —
you will obtain the full reward of your deep rumblings.
There, the courtesans, their girdles jingling with each step, their hands wearied
by playfully waving jewel-studded fly-whisks whose folds gleam with reflected lustre,
having received from you the first drops of rain, delightful as the touch of fingernails,
will cast upon you long sidelong glances like rows of bees.
Afterwards, clinging in a circle about the grove of trees tall as upraised arms,
bearing the twilight glow, red as a freshly-blossomed <s>japā</s> flower,
at the commencement of the dance, fulfill <s>Paśupati's</s> desire for a moist elephant-skin —
observed with devotion by <s>Bhavānī</s>, whose eyes are still and calm, her alarm quieted.
When women go at night to the dwellings of their lovers,
the royal highway being blocked by darkness so thick it could be pierced by a needle,
illuminate the earth for them with lightning smooth as gold on a touchstone —

children.text: toyotsargastanitamukharo mā sma bhūr viklavās tāḥ
children.translated_text: but do not, with your thunder loud from releasing rain, make them tremble with fear.
Having spent the night on some mansion-rooftop where pigeons are asleep,
your lightning-wife wearied from long dalliance,

children.text: dṛṣṭe sūrye punar api bhavān vāhayed adhvaśeṣaṃ
children.translated_text: when the sun is seen, you should once more convey what remains of the journey —
for those who have undertaken a friend's errand do not grow slack.
At that hour, the tears in the eyes of women betrayed by their lovers

children.text: śāntiṃ neyaṃ praṇayibhir ato vartma bhānos tyajāśu
children.translated_text: must be soothed by their beloveds — therefore quit the sun's path quickly,
for even the sun, returning to steal the dewy tears from the lotus-face of the water-lily pond,
would feel no small jealousy were you to obstruct his rays.
Into the deep, clear waters of that river, as into a serene heart,
even you, though merely a shadow-form, being naturally charming, will gain entrance;

children.text: tasmāt tasyāḥ kumudaviśadāny arhasi tvaṃ na dhairyān
children.translated_text: therefore you should not, out of indifference, render futile
her glances, bright as white water-lilies, that follow the darting play of restless fish.

children.text: tasyāḥ kiṃ cit karadhṛtam iva prāptavānīraśākhaṃ
children.translated_text: Having stolen her blue water-garment, leaving her hips of sandbanks exposed,
with the tips of <s>vīraṇa</s> branches seeming held in her hand,

children.text: prasthānaṃ te katham api sakhe lambamānasya bhāvi
children.translated_text: your departure, O friend, will somehow come about though you linger —
for who, having tasted her charms, is able to abandon one whose hips are sandbars?
Made holy by contact with the fragrance of the earth, released by your moisture,
drunk in by elephants with delight through the melodious sound of its passage through their trunks,

children.text: nīcair vāsyaty upajigamiṣor devapūrvaṃ giriṃ te
children.translated_text: a cool breeze will blow gently as you approach the mountain of the gods, <s>Devagiri</s>,
ripening the wild fig trees of the forest.
There, having made yourself a cloud of flowers, <s>Skanda</s>, who dwells there eternally,
you should bathe him with showers of blossoms, moist with the waters of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> —
for the protection of <s>Indra's</s> armies, that radiance was gathered

children.text: atyādityaṃ hutavahamukhe saṃbhṛtaṃ tadd hi tejaḥ
children.translated_text: in the mouth of the sacrificial fire, surpassing even the sun, by the one who bears the new moon.
The peacock feather that fell from his crest encircled by rings of light —
<s>Bhavānī</s>, out of motherly love, places it at her ear, where it touches like a blue lotus;
that peacock, its outer corners of the eyes washed bright by the moonlight from <s>Hara's</s> crescent,
you should make dance with your thunder, heavy as the rumble of seizing mountain-peaks.
Having thus worshipped the god born in the reed-thicket, and with your journey well advanced,
the path cleared for you by pairs of <s>Siddhas</s> with their <s>vīṇās</s>, fearful of water-drops,
you should descend, honoring
the fame of <s>Rantideva</s>, which has taken the form of a river-current upon the earth, born from the offering of <s>Surabhi's</s> calf.

children.text: tvayy ādātuṃ jalam avanate śārṅgiṇo varṇacaure
children.translated_text: When you bend down to take water, O stealer of colors like <s>Viṣṇu</s> who bears the bow <s>Śārṅga</s>,

children.text: tasyāḥ sindhoḥ pṛthum api tanuṃ dūrabhāvāt pravāham
children.translated_text: those who travel through the sky will see that river <s>Sindhu's</s> broad yet slender stream from afar,
gazing down from a great distance,
like a single strand of pearls upon the earth, with a large sapphire at its center.
Having crossed her, proceed onward, making your own reflection
a source of wonder for the eyes of the women of <s>Daśapura</s> —
those whose eyebrows are practiced in the play of coquetry, whose eyes flash like <s>kṛṣṇasāra</s> deer darting above their lash-fringes,
and whose beauty rivals the bees that follow a tossed <s>kunda</s> blossom.
Passing over the region of <s>Brahmāvarta</s>, its land shadowed from below by you,
visit that field of the <s>Kauravas</s>, marked by the slaughter of warriors —
where the wielder of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow rained arrows by the hundreds upon the faces of kings,

children.text: dhārāpātais tvam iva kamalāny abhyavarṣan mukhāni
children.translated_text: as you rain down streams upon lotuses.
Abandoning the <s>hālā</s> wine of desired flavour, marked with the glance-stains of <s>Revatī's</s> eyes,
the Plough-bearer, <s>Lāṅgalī</s>, turned from battle out of affection for kinsmen, and resorted to those waters —

children.text: kṛtvā tāsām abhigamam apāṃ somya sārasvatīnām
children.translated_text: having approached those waters of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, O gentle one,

children.text: antaḥsvacchas tvam api bhavitā varṇamātreṇa kṛṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: you too, though dark in hue, will become inwardly clear, dark only in appearance.
From there, proceed along the edge of the lowlands to the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s>,
descended from the king of mountains — the stairway to heaven for the sons of <s>Sagara</s>,
she who, as if laughing with her foam at the frown upon <s>Gaurī's</s> brow,
seized <s>Śambhu's</s> hair with wave-hands reaching to the moon.

children.text: tasyāḥ pātuṃ suragaja iva vyomni pūrvārdhalambī
children.translated_text: If, hanging over her from the front half of the sky like <s>Indra's</s> elephant <s>Airāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: tvaṃ ced acchasphaṭikaviśadaṃ tarkayes tiryag ambhaḥ
children.translated_text: you should draw her waters, clear as pure crystal, sideways,

children.text: saṃsarpantyā sapadi bhavataḥ srotasi cchāyayā sā
children.translated_text: then through your shadow gliding swiftly upon her current,
there would appear a charming semblance of the confluence with the <s>Yamunā</s>, though in the wrong place.
Reaching the source of that river, the pale mountain made fragrant by the musk-scent

children.text: tasyā eva prabhavam acalaṃ prāpya gauraṃ tuṣāraiḥ
children.translated_text: of deer seated upon its rocks, white with snow,
you shall proclaim, seated upon its peak to rest from the weariness of travel,
a lovely splendour comparable to the mud churned up by the bull of the three-eyed <s>Tryambaka</s>.
If on that mountain a forest fire, born from the friction of straight <s>śāla</s> trunks in the wind,
should threaten — its burden of sparks having singed the yak-tail whisks,
you are well able to quench it with thousands of water-streams —
for the wealth of the noble finds its purpose in relieving the distress of the afflicted.

children.text: ye tvāṃ muktadhvanim asahanāḥ kāyabhaṅgāya tasmin
children.translated_text: The <s>śarabhas</s> who cannot bear your loud thundering, and who in their arrogance
will leap upon you — that unassailable one — to break your body on that mountain,
you should scatter them with a shower of violent hailstones like laughter —

children.text: ke vā na syuḥ paribhavapadaṃ niṣphalārambhayatnāḥ
children.translated_text: for who would not become an object of contempt when their efforts are fruitless?
There, the footprint of the crescent-crowned one, clearly visible upon the rock,
to which the <s>Siddhas</s> perpetually bring offerings — circumambulate it with devotion bowed,
for those who behold it, their sins shaken off through the cessation of the senses upward,
become worthy of attaining the rank of the eternal <s>Gaṇas</s>, being full of faith.
The bamboos there sing sweetly, filled by the winds,
the victory over the three cities is sung by the impassioned <s>Kinnarī</s> women —

children.text: nirhrādī te muraja iva cet kandarāsu dhvaniḥ syāt
children.translated_text: if your resonant sound in the caverns should become like a <s>muraja</s> drum,

children.text: saṃgītārtho nanu paśupates tatra bhāvī samastaḥ
children.translated_text: then indeed the full musical ensemble for <s>Paśupati</s> will be complete.

children.text: prāleyādrer upataṭam atikramya tāṃs tān viśeṣān
children.translated_text: Passing beyond those various features along the slopes of the Snowy Mountain,
through <s>Krauñcarandhra</s>, the gateway of the swans, the path of <s>Bhṛgupati's</s> glory,
you shall head northward, beautiful in your lateral expanse,
dark as the upraised foot of <s>Viṣṇu</s> striding forth to subdue <s>Bali</s>.
Having traveled upward past the mountain-pass heaved apart by the arms of ten-faced <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
you shall be a guest of <s>Kailāsa</s>, that mirror of the celestial women —

children.text: śṛṅgocchrāyaiḥ kumudaviśadair yo vitatya sthitaḥ khaṃ
children.translated_text: which, with its peaks white as water-lilies, stretching high into the sky,
stands like the nightly laughter of <s>Tryambaka</s> heaped into solid form.
I foresee, when you rest upon its slope — dark as smooth collyrium,
against that mountain, white as the freshly-cut tusk-tip of an elephant —
a spectacle worthy of gazing upon with unblinking eyes:
as if a dark garment were draped upon the shoulder of the Plough-bearer, <s>Halabhṛt</s>.
If <s>Gaurī</s>, releasing the blue serpent-bracelet and taking <s>Śambhu's</s> hand,

children.text: krīḍāśaile yadi ca viharet pādacāreṇa gaurī
children.translated_text: should stroll on foot upon that pleasure-mountain,
fashion your body into curving steps, holding your inner waters still,
and become a stairway of easy, pleasant touch for her ascent.
There, inevitably producing a spray of water as you enter within,
the celestial maidens will make you into a fountain-house of channeled streams;

children.text: tābhyo mokṣas tava yadi sakhe gharmalabdhasya na syāt
children.translated_text: if there should be no release for you, O friend, from the heat thus captured,
then, playful as they are, frighten them with your thunder, harsh to the ears.
Drawing the water of <s>Mānasa</s> lake, which produces golden lotuses,
delighting <s>Airāvaṇa</s> with a momentary veil of cloud across his face,
scattering with your moist, droplet-laden winds the garments of the <s>Kalpavṛkṣa</s> trees,
enter, your shadow merging with it, that mountain clear as crystal.
Upon its lap, seeing <s>Alakā</s>, her garment of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> slipping away as from a lover,

children.text: na tvaṃ dṛṣṭvā na punar alakāṃ jñāsyase kāmacārin
children.translated_text: you shall not fail to recognize her, O wanderer at will —

children.text: yā vaḥ kāle vahati salilodgāram uccairvimānā
children.translated_text: she who at your season, from her lofty aerial palaces, sends forth showers of water,
gathering a mass of clouds like a lock of hair strung with a net of pearls.
The graceful women there, accompanied by lightning as you are, and by the rainbow — how vivid! —
beating their drums for song, producing a rich, deep resonance —
With water stored within, with gem-studded floors, with lofty spires touching the clouds,

children.text: prāsādās tvāṃ tulayitum alaṃ yatra tais tair viśeṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: the palaces there are well able to rival you, O cloud, in each of their various splendors.
A playful lotus in hand, hair interwoven with young <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) blossoms,
the beauty of their faces rendered pale by the pollen of <s>lodhra</s> flowers,
a fresh <s>kuravaka</s> blossom in the topknot, a lovely <s>śirīṣa</s> flower at the ear,

children.text: sīmante ca tvadupagamajaṃ yatra nīpaṃ vadhūnām
children.translated_text: and in the parting of their hair a <s>nīpa</s> flower born of your arrival — such are the young brides there.
Where the <s>Yakṣas</s>, arriving at mansion terraces made of white gems,
adorned with arrangements of flowers made of light and shadow, accompanied by the finest women,
drink the wine that is the fruit of love, produced by the <s>Kalpavṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling trees),
while you gently sound upon their <s>puṣkara</s> (drum-heads) with your deep rumbling.
Where, of the women sighing from the embrace of their beloveds' arms,
the languor of limbs born of lovemaking, supported by nets of threads,
is dispelled by <s>candrakānta</s> (moonstones) dripping with beads of clear water,
stimulated by moonbeams made bright after the passing of your obstruction.
Where, led by their constant motion to the topmost floors of aerial palaces,
and having instantly caused damage to the paintings with fresh drops of water,

children.text: śaṅkāspṛṣṭā iva jalamucas tvādṛśā yatra jālair
children.translated_text: clouds resembling you, as if touched by apprehension, emerge through the lattice windows
in tattered form, skillfully imitating the emission of smoke.
Where, when the garments of <s>Yakṣa</s> women, loosened by the untying of the girdle-knot,
are snatched away by eager-handed lovers,
even upon reaching the jeweled lamps with towering flames directly before them,
the fistful of powder thrown by the bashful women proves futile in extinguishing them.
Where, by <s>mandāra</s> flowers fallen from the hair due to the trembling of their gait,
by golden lotuses fashioned as ear-ornaments that have slipped off,
and by pearl necklaces with broken strings, fragrant from contact with their breasts,

children.text: naiśo mārgaḥ savitur udaye sūcyate kāminīnām
children.translated_text: the nocturnal path of amorous women is revealed at sunrise.

children.text: matvā devaṃ dhanapatisakhaṃ yatra sākṣād vasantaṃ
children.translated_text: Where, considering the lord <s>Kubera</s>, friend of <s>Śiva</s>, to be <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring) himself in person,

children.text: prāyaś cāpaṃ na vahati bhayān manmathaḥ ṣaṭpadajyam
children.translated_text: <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of Love) mostly does not carry his bow strung with bees out of fear;
his enterprise upon unerring targets of desire, aimed with glances launched with arched brows,
is accomplished entirely by the artful coquetries of clever women.
There, to the north of <s>Kubera's</s> palace, is our dwelling,

children.text: dūrāl lakṣyaṃ tad amaradhanuś cāruṇā toraṇena
children.translated_text: recognizable from afar by its beautiful archway, lovely as a rainbow;
beside which a young <s>mandāra</s> tree, raised by my beloved like a son,
bows its clusters of blossoms within reach of the hand.
And in it there is a pool with stairways lined with emerald slabs,
studded with golden lotus buds on smooth stalks of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl);
the <s>haṃsas</s> (royal geese) who have taken up residence in its waters, their sorrows gone,

children.text: na dhyāsyanti vyapagataśucas tvām api prekṣya haṃsāḥ
children.translated_text: will not think of <s>Mānasa</s> lake nearby, even upon seeing you.
On its bank stands a pleasure-hill with a heaped peak of fine sapphires,
beautiful to behold with its encircling golden plantain trees.

children.text: madgehinyāḥ priya iti sakhe cetasā kātareṇa
children.translated_text: O friend, with an anxious heart that calls it 'my wife's beloved,'
seeing you nearby with lightning flashing at your side, I remember that very hill.
A red <s>aśoka</s> with trembling young shoots and a lovely <s>kesara</s> tree are there,
near the <s>kuravaka</s> hedge and the <s>mādhavī</s> bower;

children.text: ekaḥ sakhyās tava saha mayā vāmapādābhilāṣī
children.translated_text: the one, my friend, desires the touch of her left foot along with me,
while the other craves the wine of her mouth, under the pretext of the pregnancy-craving.
And in the midst of these stands a golden perch with a crystal slab,
bound at the base with gems of subdued bamboo-like luster;
made to dance by my beloved with rhythmic beats lovely with jingling bracelets,

children.text: yām adhyāste divasavigame nīlakaṇṭhaḥ suhṛd vaḥ
children.translated_text: upon which at the close of day sits a peacock, your friend.
By these signs stored in your heart, O noble one, you should recognize the house,
and also by seeing the painted figures of a conch and lotus at the sides of the door.
It is now of diminished splendor, surely because of my absence —

children.text: sūryāpāye na khalu kamalaṃ puṣyati svām abhikhyām
children.translated_text: indeed, the lotus does not flourish in its own glory when the sun is gone.
Having swiftly assumed the slender form of a young elephant for the sake of quick descent,
and having settled on the lovely ridge of the pleasure-hill first described,
you should cast into the inner chamber a lightning-glance of faint, flickering light,
resembling the play of a swarm of fireflies.
Slender, dark-complexioned, with teeth sharp as the edge of a blade, with lips like ripe <s>bimba</s> fruit,
slim at the waist, with the glance of a startled doe, with a deep navel,
slow in her gait from the weight of her hips, slightly bent by the fullness of her breasts —

children.text: yā tatra syād yuvativiṣaye sṛṣṭir ādyeva dhātuḥ
children.translated_text: she who is there would seem to be the Creator's first creation among women.

children.text: tāṃ jānīyāḥ parimitakathāṃ jīvitaṃ me dvitīyaṃ
children.translated_text: Know her, who speaks but little, as my second life;
like a lone <s>cakravākī</s> (ruddy goose) when I, her companion, have gone far away.
In these days that pass so heavily with intense longing, I imagine the young woman
to have become like a lotus-plant crushed by frost, or of some other altered form.
Surely her face, with eyes swollen from violent weeping,
with lips discolored from the warmth of many sighs,
resting on her hand, its expression obscured by the hanging of disheveled locks,
bears the wretchedness of the moon whose radiance is marred by your approach.

children.text: āloke te nipatati purā sā balivyākulā vā
children.translated_text: Perhaps when your light first falls, she will be busy with the evening offering,
or drawing a likeness of me, its thinness revealing her separation, discernible only to the heart,
or asking the sweet-voiced <s>śārikā</s> (mynah bird) in its cage,

children.text: kac cid bhartuḥ smarasi nibhṛte tvaṃ hi tasya priyeti
children.translated_text: 'O gentle one, do you remember your master? For you were indeed his beloved.'

children.text: utsaṅge vā malinavasane somya nikṣipya vīṇāṃ
children.translated_text: Or, placing the <s>vīṇā</s> on her lap in its soiled covering, O gentle cloud,
wishing to sing a song composed with words bearing my name,

children.text: tantrīr ārdrā nayanasalilaiḥ sārayitvā kathaṃ cid
children.translated_text: having somehow managed to tune the strings wet with tears from her eyes,

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ svayam api kṛtāṃ mūrcchanāṃ vismarantī
children.translated_text: she forgets again and again the melody she herself has composed.
Or counting the remaining months of the appointed term reckoned from the day of departure,
laying out on the ground with flowers placed on the threshold,
or savoring in her heart the first stirrings of the thought of reunion —
these, for the most part, are the diversions of women during separation from their lovers.

children.text: ādye baddhā virahadivase yā śikhā dāma hitvā
children.translated_text: The single braid that was bound on the first day of separation, the ornamental cord cast aside,
which is to be unloosed by me, with sorrow dissolved, at the end of the curse —
she repeatedly smooths it with untrimmed nails as it chafes her,
pushing it from the hard, uneven curve of her cheek with her hand.

children.text: savyāpārām ahani na tathā khedayed viprayogaḥ
children.translated_text: Separation would not so much afflict her during the day when she is occupied;

children.text: śaṅke rātrau gurutaraśucaṃ nirvinodāṃ sakhīṃ te
children.translated_text: I fear that at night, without diversion, your friend bears a heavier grief.

children.text: matsaṃdeśaiḥ sukhayitum ataḥ paśya sādhvīṃ niśīthe
children.translated_text: Therefore, to comfort the faithful one with my message, observe her at midnight,
wakeful, stationed at the window near her bed upon the ground.
Emaciated beyond measure, lying on one side of the bed of separation,
like the slender crescent of the waning moon at the eastern horizon,
'How can union with me come about, even in a dream?' — thus
longing for sleep whose scope is blocked by tears pressing from her eyes.
Tossing aside with sighs that torment her tender lower lip
the coarse hair, surely hanging to her cheeks, unwashed since her ritual bath,

children.text: nītā rātriḥ kṣaṇa iva mayā sārdham icchāratair yā
children.translated_text: she who once spent nights like a moment with me in the pleasures of desire,
now passes them on the bed of separation with hot tears.
The ambrosia-cool rays of the moon entering through the lattice window —
her gaze, which moved toward them with former affection, turns back again just the same;
covering her eyes in distress with eyelashes heavy with tears,

children.text: sābhre 'hnīva sthalakamalinīṃ na prabuddhāṃ na suptām
children.translated_text: like a day-lotus plant on a cloudy day, neither fully awake nor asleep.

children.text: jāne sakhyās tava mayi manaḥ saṃbhṛtasneham asmād
children.translated_text: I know that my friend's heart has cherished love for me; therefore
I imagine her to be in such a state during this first separation.

children.text: vācālaṃ māṃ na khalu subhagaṃmanyabhāvaḥ karoti
children.translated_text: It is not the conceit of one who thinks himself fortunate that makes me speak so;

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ te nikhilam acirād bhrātar uktaṃ mayā yat
children.translated_text: all that I have said, O brother, will soon be evident to you directly.
That frail woman, wearing only a thin garment, her ornaments laid aside,
placing her body repeatedly on the lap of the couch, weary with sorrow upon sorrow —

children.text: tvām apy asraṃ navajalamayaṃ mocayiṣyaty avaśyaṃ
children.translated_text: she will surely cause even you to shed tears of fresh rainwater;
for generally, every being whose inner soul is tender becomes disposed to compassion.
Her sidelong glance obstructed by disheveled locks, devoid of collyrium's luster,
its playful movement of the brows forgotten even at the rebuke of <s>Madhu</s> (Spring),

children.text: tvayy āsanne nayanam uparispandi śaṅke mṛgākṣyā
children.translated_text: when you draw near, I believe the eye of that doe-eyed one, trembling upward,
will attain the beauty of a blue lotus agitated by the darting of a fish.
Her left thigh, being freed from the nail-marks made by me,
its familiar pearl-net ornament abandoned, relinquished by the course of fate,
worthy of the massage of my hands after the culmination of love —
that thigh, fair as a fresh plantain stem, will regain its trembling.

children.text: tasmin kāle jalada dayitā labdhanidrā yadi syād
children.translated_text: At that hour, O cloud, if my beloved should have found sleep,
attend upon her and restrain your thunder for just one watch of the night.

children.text: mā bhūd asyāḥ praṇayini mayi svapnalabdhe kathaṃ cit
children.translated_text: Let it not happen that in her dream, somehow obtaining me, her lover,
the tight embrace, with the knot of her vine-like arms clasped around my neck, be suddenly broken.
Having awakened her with a breeze cooled by your own water-drops,
and having reassured her together with fresh <s>mālatī</s> blossoms at the lattice windows,
her gaze fixed upon the window sheltered by you with lightning within,
you should begin to address the proud one in words of steady thunder.

children.text: bhartur mitraṃ priyam avidhave viddhi mām ambuvāhaṃ
children.translated_text: Know me, O faithful wife, as the cloud, the dear friend of your husband,
come to your presence bearing his message held in my heart,

children.text: yo vṛndāni tvarayati pathi śrāmyatāṃ proṣitānāṃ
children.translated_text: I who hasten the footsteps of weary travelers on the road, longing for those far from home.
with deep, smooth sounds, eager [as if] to loosen the braids of young women —
When you are thus described, she, like <s>Maithilī</s> (Sītā) turning upward [at the sight of] the Son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>),
seeing you, her heart heaving with longing, and honoring [you],

children.text: śroṣyaty asmāt param avahitā somya sīmantinīnāṃ
children.translated_text: will listen henceforth attentively, O gentle one — for among faithful wives,

children.text: kāntodantaḥ suhṛdupanataḥ saṃgamāt kiṃ cid ūnaḥ
children.translated_text: news of a beloved brought by a friend is only slightly less than [actual] union.

children.text: tām āyuṣmān mama ca vacanād ātmanā copakartuṃ
children.translated_text: Long-lived one, tell her this, both on my behalf and to comfort her on your own —
'Your companion, dwelling in the hermitage of <s>Rāmagiri</s>,

children.text: avyāpannaḥ kuśalam abale pṛcchati tvāṃ viyuktaḥ
children.translated_text: unharmed, asks after your well-being, O gentle one, though separated [from you] —
this alone is the first prayer of living beings for whom misfortunes come easily.'

children.text: aṅgenāṅgaṃ tanu ca tanunā gāḍhataptena taptaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Limb against limb — slender with slender, burning with deeply burning,
tearful with flowing tears, ceaselessly longing with longing,
sighing hot sighs with one who sighs even more — though far away,

children.text: saṃkalpais te viśati vidhinā vairiṇā ruddhamārgaḥ
children.translated_text: through imagination he enters you, his path blocked by hostile fate.'

children.text: śabdākhyeyaṃ yad api kila te yaḥ sakhīnāṃ purastāt
children.translated_text: 'That which, though expressible in words, was formerly whispered in your ear
before your friends, trembling [at your ear], out of greed to touch your face —
he, now beyond the range of hearing and unreachable by eyes,
through my mouth speaks this to you, composed in words fashioned by longing:'
'In dark [rain-clouds] I see your limbs, in the glance of a startled doe your gaze,
in the moon your cheek's radiance, in the heavy tail-feathers of peacocks your hair,
in the slender ripples of rivers your playful brow-movements —

children.text: hantaikasthaṃ kva cid api na te bhīru sādṛśyam asti
children.translated_text: alas, O timid one, nowhere is your likeness found in any single place!'
'Having drawn you in a picture with mineral pigments on a rock-slab, angry from love's quarrel,

children.text: ātmānaṃ te caraṇapatitaṃ yāvad icchāmi kartum
children.translated_text: as I wish to portray myself fallen at your feet —

children.text: asrais tāvan muhur upacitair dṛṣṭir ālipyate me
children.translated_text: my vision is blurred again and again by welling tears;

children.text: krūras tasminn api na sahate saṃgamaṃ nau kṛtāntaḥ
children.translated_text: cruel fate does not permit even our union in a painting!'
'When I stretch my arms toward the sky to embrace you pitilessly,

children.text: labdhāyās te katham api sati svapnasaṃdarśaneṣu
children.translated_text: having somehow obtained you in the visions of dreams —

children.text: paśyantīnāṃ na khalu bahuśo na sthalīdevatānāṃ
children.translated_text: seeing this, surely not infrequently do the guardian goddesses of the place
shed tear-drops, thick as pearls, upon the tree-shoots.'
'Those winds of the Snowy Mountain (<s>Tuṣāragiri</s>) that blow from the south,
fragrant with the sap-flow from freshly split leaf-sheaths of <s>devadāru</s> trees —
'I embrace them, O virtuous one,

children.text: pūrvaspṛṣṭaṃ yadi kila bhaved aṅgam ebhis taveti
children.translated_text: thinking: perhaps your limbs were previously touched by these.'

children.text: saṃkṣipyeran kṣaṇa iva kathaṃ dīrghayāmās triyāmāḥ
children.translated_text: 'How could the long nights, each watch seeming endless, be compressed into a mere moment?

children.text: sarvāvasthāsv ahar api kathaṃ mandamandātapaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: How could the day, in every state, have but a slow, gentle sun?
Thus my mind, O you of restless eyes, is full of longings hard to fulfill,
made shelterless by the burning pangs of separation from you.'

children.text: nanv ātmānaṃ bahu vigaṇayann ātmanā nāvalambe
children.translated_text: 'Though I value my own life greatly, I do not rely upon myself for support;

children.text: tat kalyāṇi tvam api sutarāṃ mā gamaḥ kātaratvam
children.translated_text: therefore, O auspicious one, do not you either fall into excessive despair.

children.text: kasyātyantaṃ sukham upanataṃ duḥkham ekāntato vā
children.translated_text: To whom has unalloyed happiness come? Or unmitigated sorrow?

children.text: nīcair gacchaty upari ca daśā cakranemikrameṇa
children.translated_text: Fortune rises and falls in turn, like the rim of a wheel.'
'My curse will end when the Bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) rises from his serpent-couch.

children.text: māsān anyān gamaya caturo locane mīlayitvā
children.translated_text: Pass the remaining four months with eyes closed [in patience];

children.text: paścād āvāṃ virahaguṇitaṃ taṃ tam ātmābhilāṣaṃ
children.translated_text: thereafter, we two shall fulfill each and every desire of our hearts, multiplied by separation,
during nights lit by the moonlight of mature autumn.'

children.text: bhūyaś cāha tvam api śayane kaṇṭhalagnā purā me
children.translated_text: And again he said: 'You too, formerly clinging to my neck upon our bed,

children.text: nidrāṃ gatvā kim api rudatī sasvanaṃ viprabuddhā
children.translated_text: having fallen asleep, weeping for some reason, awakened with sobs —

children.text: sāntarhāsaṃ kathitam asakṛt pṛcchataś ca tvayā me
children.translated_text: when I asked you repeatedly with a hidden smile,

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ svapne kitava ramayan kām api tvaṃ mayeti
children.translated_text: [you said:] "I saw you in a dream, O rogue — making love to some other woman!"'
'Therefore, knowing me to be well from the token of recognition [I send],

children.text: mā kaulīnād asitanayane mayy aviśvāsinī bhūḥ
children.translated_text: do not, O dark-eyed one, become distrustful of me out of [your family's] good breeding.

children.text: snehān āhuḥ kim api virahahrāsinas te hy abhogād
children.translated_text: Love, they say, when diminished by separation, somehow [grows again]; for in the absence [of the beloved,]
when the desired object is [remembered], it swells with richer passion and becomes a flood of love.'

children.text: kac cit somya vyavasitam idaṃ bandhukṛtyaṃ tvayā me
children.translated_text: 'O gentle one, will you refuse to do this service of a friend that I have resolved upon?

children.text: pratyākhyātuṃ na khalu bhavato dhīratāṃ tarkayāmi
children.translated_text: Surely I do not doubt your steadfastness;
even without being asked, you give water to the <s>cātaka</s> birds [who cry for rain] —
for the true response to those who are dear is indeed the fulfillment of their desired purpose.'
'Having done this kindness for me, one who has taken the path of an improper request,

children.text: sauhārdād vā vidhura iti vā mayy anukrośabuddhyā
children.translated_text: whether out of friendship, or because I am wretched, or from compassion toward me —

children.text: iṣṭān deśān vicara jalada prāvṛṣā saṃbhṛtaśrīr
children.translated_text: wander through beloved lands, O cloud, your splendor replenished by the rains;

children.text: mā bhūd evaṃ kṣaṇam api ca te vidyutā viprayogaḥ
children.translated_text: and may there never be separation from your lightning, even for a moment.'
